planetIntros.intro: The Sun is your essential self, your identity and the spirit you lead with. It shows how each of you shines and takes up space.
Your Moon shows how you feel, what comforts you, how you care for yourself and others, how you react when you are hurt, and what helps you recover after stress.
Mercury rules communication, intellect, and reasoning. It shows how each of you thinks, talks, and needs to be understood.
Venus shows how you show someone they matter, what makes you feel appreciated, and what you notice when deciding whether someone’s care can be trusted.
Mars is the planet of drive and conflict, the warrior and the protector. It shows how each of you goes after what you want and handles anger.
Jupiter is the planet of expansion and good fortune. It shows how each of you grows, hopes, and finds meaning.
Saturn rules structure, discipline, and limits. It shows how each of you handles responsibility and the long game.

evidenceRows.youEvidence: Your Moon is in Aries, meaning you deal with a feeling by doing something about it, fast, and you'd rather be angry than helpless. This is learned behavior. If you grew up around someone quick to flare, anger was probably the feeling that got results, so you learned to stand up for yourself right away instead of waiting to see how bad it would get. You still need wins, because sitting still with a problem feels worse to you than picking the wrong fight. When you're upset, you react first and deal with the damage later.
friendEvidenceVariants: Their Moon is in Taurus, meaning they regulate their emotions through their body and their routine, and no words work as fast as food, touch, or familiar surroundings. This is learned behavior. If the people around them growing up were stable, or if they badly needed them to be, comfort and consistency became their proof that things would be okay. They still need life to stay predictable where it counts, because change at the wrong time can shake them more than they show. When they're upset, they go still, keep their day exactly the same, and come around on their own schedule, not anyone else's.

Their Moon is in Gemini, meaning they work out what they feel by talking about it, and a feeling they can't put into words doesn't feel finished. This is learned behavior. If the people around them growing up were lively but hard to predict, they learned to keep talking, keep asking, and keep things moving, because conversation was how they found out where they stood. They still need stimulation, because boredom weighs on them more than most problems do. When they're upset, they get chatty and clever instead of sad, and they can explain a feeling ten ways before they actually feel it once.

Their Moon is in Cancer, meaning they feel things deeply and keep them protected, and home is less a place to them than the feeling of being safe with their people. This is learned behavior. If care in their house growing up came on strong, or came and went, they learned to hold their people close and to look after everyone as a way of belonging. They still need to feel safe before they can be honest, because tone reaches them before words do. When they're upset, they pull in without announcing it, take care of everyone anyway, and wait to see who notices.

Their Moon is in Leo, meaning they light up when someone is genuinely glad to see them, and affection that never gets said doesn't fully count. This is learned behavior. If attention in their house growing up came in big moments or not at all, they learned that being noticed meant being loved, so they give with their whole heart and pay close attention to what comes back. They still need appreciation, because giving to people who don't notice wears them out faster than the giving itself. When they're upset, they go quiet and proud, and they wait for the apology instead of asking for it.

Their Moon is in Virgo, meaning they calm down by being useful, and a fixed problem soothes them more than comforting words do. This is learned behavior. If the standards around them growing up were high or hard to hit, they learned that being helpful and getting things right kept them safe, so they got very good at spotting what's wrong before anyone else does. They still need to feel useful, because sitting on their hands is its own kind of struggle.
